chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Pay and bandmates at Suntaug Lake Inn
summary: He explains pay rose from room and board to $250-300 a week, and names Carl White, Leroy Tibbs, Clarence Cummings and Willie Lynch.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But all them people come down here today and they tip $10. Man, you know, we used to make $35 a night -- five of us, and we each made $35 a night.

This was around '15 or '14. And we were, at first, we went down there, we were working for room and board -- $15 a week room and board. Then we got up to $45, room and board. And we used to make from $250 to $300 a week.
Do you remember any of the guys who were with you in those days?

Yes, there was Carl White -- he played the banjo and he sang. Leroy Tibbs played the tenor saxophone. Clarence Cummings, he played the violin, and Willie Lynch, he played drums. You probably know Willie Lynch, he used to play at the Savoy, he had that big band, you know, when the Savoy opened? Willie Lynch had the band.
I was just gonna ask you did any of those guys ever make it to New York?
Yeah, they came here to New York.
Willie came. But the other guys, I think they stayed in Boston.
